question: Which of the following is / are meant for promoting the ideals of social and economic democracy?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs)** in the Indian Constitution promote the ideals of social and economic democracy.
 
• **DPSPs:**
 
 
• These principles are** found in Part IV of the Constitution.**
 
• They are **instructions to the state on how to formulate policies and enact laws.**
 
• They are intended to establish a welfare state in India.
 
• They are **non-justiciable**, meaning they cannot be enforced by the courts.
 
• They are fundamental to the governance of the country.
 
• They** impose a moral obligation on the state to apply them.**
 
• They are **classified into three broad categories: socialistic, Gandhian, and liberal-intellectual.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** concept of single citizenship in India was inspired by the British Constitution**
 
• The concept of** Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution** was borrowed from the Soviet Constitution of the USSR (now Russia)
 
 
• The Fundamental Duties** were added to the Indian Constitution in 1976 by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act**, on the recommendation of Sardar Swaran Singh. 
 
 
 
• **Co-operative Societies**
 
 
• **​**A **co-operative society is a voluntary association of people who join together to achieve common economic**, social, and cultural goals.
 
• The main objective of a co-operative society is to support its members, especially those from poorer sections of society.
